changelog: 1.0.0 first release as an unreleased draft; 1.1.0 re-publishes it under a new version because the boundary ledger and the CBAM validation restatement changed after the acceptance run (docs/CBAM_IRON_STEEL_BF_BOF_SEED_V1.md §9.7). Original 1.0.0 release note: 1.0.0 first release for the BF-BOF crude steel seed. Nineteen clauses, all anchored in the 2026-09-19 canonical texts, with the ST-12 and ST-14 readings taken from the base regulation and the rest from Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2547. Two defects, five verification gaps and eleven modeling gaps are registered rather than smoothed over: the Annex III cross-reference defect D-S1, the hydrogen membership key defect D-S2, and MG-S01 to MG-S11. The seed's arithmetic profile deliberately binds no combustion or stoichiometry check, because ST-08 puts every crude steel source stream under the mass balance method.

canonicalization.algorithm: drop script/style blocks, replace remaining tags and character entities with a space, collapse whitespace runs, trim; SHA-256 over UTF-8 bytes
canonicalization.reason: EUR-Lex HTML embeds a per-request analytics token, so raw byte hashes are not reproducible
canonicalization.offset_convention: a bare @NNNN offsets into S3, the main source of this seed; every other source carries a prefix, so @s1:NNNN offsets into S1
canonicalization.retrieval_constraint: repeated same-session fetches eventually return HTTP 202 with an empty body; see retrieval_attempts

retrieval_attempts.detail: all four URLs returned HTTP 202 with an empty body behind an AWS WAF challenge (x-amzn-waf-action: challenge, x-cache: Error from cloudfront); publications.europa.eu timed out from this host and the PDF endpoint was closed by the server. Every record has canonical_text_sha256 null, because an empty body's hash must never be written as if a text had been retrieved.
retrieval_attempts.consequence: the two hashes in the sources block above remain the 2026-09-19 authoring-time readings and were not re-verified by this attempt; that is gap GS-02
retrieval_attempts.not_blocked: every crude steel boundary, precursor, activity level and mass balance clause used by this seed is in the already cached S3 text, so the failure blocks only the default value numbers, which is modeling gap MG-S05

verification.method: each quote is checked to sit verbatim at its declared character offset in the cached canonical text, by tmp/segment9h_37_author_steel_clause_mapping.py at authoring time and by tmp/segment9h_02_check_steel_offsets.py over the contract document

runs.against: the cached canonical texts of S1 and S3 at the offsets recorded in this file
runs.result: 79 quotes / 85 offset markers / 0 problems, of which the 19 clause quotes above and every parameters and boundary citation

runs.against: a fresh retrieval of the same two URLs
runs.result: not obtained; HTTP 202 empty body, so no hash was re-verified (gap GS-02)

not_checked_by_substring_search: the occurrence counts of 2601 11 00, 2701, 2704 00 00, 2711, 2716 00 00 and 7204 quoted in the contract document sections 4 and 6 were computed once against the canonical texts during authoring and are not independently re-derivable from this file

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/956 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism
sources.entry_into_force: day following publication in the Official Journal (Article 36(1))
used_by_this_seed_for: ST-12 Article 7(1) and the Annex II direct-only listing of Chapter 72
ST-13 and ST-14 Annex I membership of the candidate input codes
the reporting period clause and the default value deferral sentence

sources.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2547 of 10 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the methods for the calculation of emissions embedded in goods
sources.entry_into_force: third day following publication in the Official Journal (Article 16), i.e. 2025-12-25
sources.application: Article 16 states no separate application date
used_by_this_seed_for: the whole boundary, functional unit, precursor, activity level and mass balance reading of crude steel, i.e. every clause except ST-12 and ST-14

clauses.anchor: The functional units for iron and steel should be determined following the general rule
clauses.quote: The functional units for iron and steel should be determined following the general rule, since the CN codes are already allowing differentiation in the calculation of embedded emissions.
clauses.model_role: goods_identity: the functional unit is one tonne of the CN code good, here crude steel under CN 7207, with no element-content conversion of any kind. This is the clause that makes the seed's kg-per-tonne constant the only unit bridge in the model
clauses.required_evidence: the recital quoted above plus the general functional unit rule of Article 4(1) that it points at
clauses.validation: functional_unit.denominator must be a reference product output port of this model and kg_per_tonne must be a declared package constant; no mass floor basis may appear anywhere in the boundary or the package
clauses.acceptance_case: a boundary that attaches an element-content denominator to crude steel is refused at build time

clauses.locator: Annex I point 2, Table 1, Iron and Steel block
clauses.anchor: 2601 12 00 – Agglomerated iron ores and concentrates, other than roasted iron pyrites Sintered Ore Carbon dioxide
clauses.quote: 2601 12 00 – Agglomerated iron ores and concentrates, other than roasted iron pyrites Sintered Ore Carbon dioxide
clauses.model_role: goods_identity: the aggregated goods category of the declared good is Crude steel and its greenhouse gas list is CO2 only. The sinter row is quoted in the same block because it fixes which category the in-house sinter belongs to
clauses.required_evidence: the Table 1 rows for the Iron and Steel block, read together with the crude steel row at offset 51389
clauses.validation: boundaries/cbam.json goods_identity.cn_code, aggregated_goods_category and greenhouse_gases must equal the table reading; the set may not be widened by inference from the route
clauses.acceptance_case: a seed that lists nitrous oxide among the counted gases for crude steel is refused

clauses.locator: Annex I point 3.11.1, Sintered Ore special provisions
clauses.anchor: This aggregated goods category includes all kinds of iron ore pellet production (for sale of pellets as well as for direct use in the same installation) and sinter production.
clauses.quote: This aggregated goods category includes all kinds of iron ore pellet production (for sale of pellets as well as for direct use in the same installation) and sinter production.
clauses.model_role: process_identity: sintering is its own production process with its own system boundary, so the seed models ore-sintering as a separate graph node rather than folding it into the furnace
clauses.required_evidence: the 3.11.1 sentence above plus the 3.11.2 monitoring sentence at offset 65969
clauses.validation: the sinter node must carry its own carbonate decomposition and solid fuel emission ports; a model that emits all sinter carbon dioxide from the furnace node fails the role coverage check
clauses.acceptance_case: removing the sinter carbonate port leaves a mandatory role unanswered and blocks import

clauses.locator: Annex I point 3.13.1, Pig Iron special provisions
clauses.anchor: In integrated steel plants, liquid pig iron (‘hot metal’) directly charged to the oxygen converter is the product which separates the production process for pig iron from the production process of crude steel.
clauses.quote: In integrated steel plants, liquid pig iron (‘hot metal’) directly charged to the oxygen converter is the product which separates the production process for pig iron from the production process of crude steel.
clauses.model_role: graph_edge_identity: hot metal is the named split stream, so the model must carry one identifiable hot metal exchange from the blast furnace node to the converter node rather than an anonymous bulk transfer
clauses.validation: model/graph.json must contain exactly one hot metal provider/consumer pair, and the CBAM boundary must dispose of both of its ports as internal transfers of the monitored boundary
clauses.acceptance_case: a model that names hot metal as a precursor while it is an internal edge of the same monitored boundary is refused by the precursor source gate

clauses.locator: Annex I point 3.13.1, third sentence, referring to Article 4(9)
clauses.anchor: Where the installation does not sell or transfer pig iron to other installations, a joint production process including crude steel can be established making subject to the rules of Article 4.
clauses.quote: Where the installation does not sell or transfer pig iron to other installations, a joint production process including crude steel can be established making subject to the rules of Article 4.
clauses.model_role: boundary_orientation: a joint production process is permitted, not required. This seed takes the permission and monitors the five processes as one production process boundary, which is the reading that empties the precursor bucket; the alternative reading, where sinter and hot metal each carry their own specific embedded emissions, is registered as modeling gap MG-S02
clauses.required_evidence: the 3.13.1 sentence above plus Article 4(9) at offset 25670, quoted as the joint production rule it invokes
clauses.validation: consolidation_policy.in_boundary_process_uuids must list every process node of the model, and the two in-house precursor candidates must be disposed of as internal transfers rather than as counted or as precursor mass
clauses.acceptance_case: a boundary that lists only some of the model's processes inside the monitored boundary while netting transfers across the omission is refused

clauses.locator: Annex I point 3.15.1, crude steel system boundary, hot metal branch
clauses.anchor: if the process starts from hot metal (liquid pig iron), the system boundary shall include the basic oxygen converter, vacuum degassing, secondary metallurgy, argon oxygen decarburisation / vacuum oxygen decarburisation, continuous casting or ingot casting, where relevant hot-rolling or forging, and all necessary auxiliary activities such as transfers, re-heating, and flue gas cleaning
clauses.quote: if the process starts from hot metal (liquid pig iron), the system boundary shall include the basic oxygen converter, vacuum degassing, secondary metallurgy, argon oxygen decarburisation / vacuum oxygen decarburisation, continuous casting or ingot casting, where relevant hot-rolling or forging, and all necessary auxiliary activities such as transfers, re-heating, and flue gas cleaning
clauses.model_role: mandatory_role_check: the enumerated activity list is the checklist every crude steel model is measured against. The seed authors converter, secondary metallurgy with degassing and continuous casting as nodes, and carries hot rolling plus flue gas cleaning as declared slots with no exchange, which is modeling gap MG-S09
clauses.required_evidence: the 3.15.1 enumeration above, plus the 3.15.2.1 basic oxygen steelmaking enumeration at offset 72960 and the 3.15.1 sentence at offset 73489 that puts carbon entering in scrap and alloys under a mass balance
clauses.validation: every activity named by the enumeration must resolve to a node, to a port, or to a slot entry that states it is not authored; an activity that resolves to nothing at all blocks import
clauses.acceptance_case: adding a furnace or a caster changes the mandatory role answer set, which the coverage report must restate; a silent omission fails the check

clauses.anchor: only primary hot-rolling and rough shaping by forging to obtain the semi-finished products under CN codes 7207 , 7218 and 7224 are included in this aggregated goods category.
clauses.quote: only primary hot-rolling and rough shaping by forging to obtain the semi-finished products under CN codes 7207 , 7218 and 7224 are included in this aggregated goods category. All other rolling and forging processes are included in the aggregated goods category ‘iron or steel products’.
clauses.model_role: boundary_extents: the crude steel category ends at the semi-finished product, so finishing rolling is a different aggregated goods category and may not be added to this model to make the numbers look like a plant. The seed's declared good is the continuous casting slab, CN 7207, which the bullet names
clauses.required_evidence: the bullet above plus the 3.16.2 iron or steel products boundary at offset 74694, which is the category the omitted activities belong to
clauses.validation: model/graph.json must stop at the caster; a node whose technology description is finishing rolling would change the aggregated goods category and is out of scope for this version
clauses.acceptance_case: the registered modeling gap MG-S01 keeps the exclusion visible instead of letting it read as a complete steel plant

clauses.locator: Annex II point B.3.2, Mass balance method
clauses.model_role: arithmetic_method: this is the only emission derivation the seed uses. Carbon in, carbon out in product and slag, the difference times f gives the carbon dioxide. Fuels and process materials are treated the same way, which is why the model has no fuel duty, no net calorific value slot and no oxidation factor
clauses.required_evidence: the B.3.2 heading above, plus the method sentence that follows it in the same text, the negative activity rule at offset 108148 and the molar ratio constant at offset 105374
clauses.validation: parameters/carbon-content.json must state the carbon book per port and the factor as the quoted constant with its offset; the builder must not find any EF times NCV times OF chain in this seed's profile, because the arithmetic_checks block names only mass_balance and result_expectations
clauses.acceptance_case: a steel seed that declares the hydrogen seed's combustion check fails the profile gate, which is the intended reading of this clause

clauses.locator: Annex IV point 2, sector-specific parameters, Crude steel column
clauses.anchor: Crude steel — The main reducing agent of the precursor, if known. — Mass % of Mn, Cr, Ni, total of other alloy elements. — Tonnes scrap used for producing 1 t crude steel. — % of scrap that is pre-consumer scrap.
clauses.quote: Crude steel — The main reducing agent of the precursor, if known. — Mass % of Mn, Cr, Ni, total of other alloy elements. — Tonnes scrap used for producing 1 t crude steel. — % of scrap that is pre-consumer scrap.
clauses.model_role: declaration_fields: the crude steel report asks for four data items and none of them is an emission factor or an element-content denominator. The seed carries them as empty activity slots in parameters/sector-specific-declaration-parameters.json with the reason each one is empty, which is modeling gap MG-S04 for the scrap split
clauses.required_evidence: the Crude steel column above plus the adjacent Sintered Ore column reading N.a. at offset 234898, which is the evidence that no element-content floor exists on this side
clauses.validation: every one of the four fields must be present with a null value and a stated reason; filling any of them with a plausible default would turn a declaration field into an invented factor
clauses.acceptance_case: a package that reads one of these fields as a calculation input is refused because no code path consumes them

clauses.locator: Annex I point 3.13.2.1, blast furnace route system boundary
clauses.anchor: all processes directly or indirectly linked to the production processes emitting CO 2 from fuels and reducing agents such as coke, coke dust, coal, fuel oils, plastic wastes, natural gas, wood wastes, charcoal, as well as from waste gases such as coke oven gas, blast furnace gas or converter gas
clauses.quote: all processes directly or indirectly linked to the production processes emitting CO 2 from fuels and reducing agents such as coke, coke dust, coal, fuel oils, plastic wastes, natural gas, wood wastes, charcoal, as well as from waste gases such as coke oven gas, blast furnace gas or converter gas
clauses.model_role: source_stream_set: the furnace boundary covers every carbon-bearing input, and the waste gases are named as part of the same system, which is why the model treats furnace gas as an exchange inside the monitored boundary rather than as an emission. Carbon that leaves as exported gas is not subtracted by this version, which is modeling gap MG-S11
clauses.required_evidence: the 3.13.2.1 first bullet above, read with the 3.15.2.1 bullet at offset 73489 that puts scrap and alloy carbon under the same mass balance
clauses.validation: every carbon-bearing technosphere input of the furnace node must appear in the carbon book of parameters/carbon-content.json with a port, a carbon mass and a destination emission port
clauses.acceptance_case: an added fuel input with no carbon book row leaves the book unbalanced and fails the ledger check, which is how a missing emission source is caught rather than lost

clauses.locator: Annex II point G, standard factors for installation level direct emissions
clauses.anchor: G. STANDARD FACTORS USED IN THE MONITORING OF DIRECT EMISSIONS AT INSTALLATION LEVEL
clauses.quote: G. STANDARD FACTORS USED IN THE MONITORING OF DIRECT EMISSIONS AT INSTALLATION LEVEL
clauses.model_role: factor_source_registry: point G is a numeric table of standard factors, with Table 1 for fuel emission factors and net calorific values, Table 3 for carbonate stoichiometric factors, Table 5 for the iron and steel process material factors and Table 6 for global warming potentials. The seed cites the rows it needs and takes no number from them, because its emissions come from the mass balance of ST-08
clauses.required_evidence: the point G heading above plus the table headings at offsets 186576, 187689 and 188255 and the cited rows recorded in parameters/annex-ii-point-g-standard-factors.json
clauses.validation: a factor citation must carry annex, section, table number, row label, offset and the source text hash; the builder must find no emission factor literal outside those citation records
clauses.acceptance_case: this seed's arithmetic profile binds no combustion check, so a factor cannot leak into a numerator; the citation table is what a later version that models fuel duty would read

clauses.anchor: Embedded emissions in goods shall be calculated pursuant to the methods set out in Annex IV. For goods listed in Annex II only direct emissions shall be calculated and taken into account.
clauses.quote: Article 7 Calculation of embedded emissions 1. Embedded emissions in goods shall be calculated pursuant to the methods set out in Annex IV. For goods listed in Annex II only direct emissions shall be calculated and taken into account.
clauses.model_role: component_set: crude steel sits in Annex II, so the CBAM result has exactly one component, the direct carbon dioxide term. There is no indirect electricity term and no precursor term, and the ammonia seed's three-component profile must not be copied here
clauses.required_evidence: Article 7(1) above plus the Annex II Iron and steel block at offset 149771 that lists Chapter 72 as a direct-only good
clauses.validation: the method package must carry formula_graph.calculation actual_specific_embedded_emissions_multi_process_direct_only and must carry no boundary_schema.emission_components block and no mass floor basis; the acceptance ledger must have one emission component row, of kind direct_co2
clauses.acceptance_case: adding an indirect electricity component to the crude steel package is refused by the profile gate, not by a review comment

clauses.anchor: ‘precursor’ means any input material into a production process included in the list of goods set out in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2023/956;
clauses.quote: ‘precursor’ means any input material into a production process included in the list of goods set out in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2023/956;
clauses.model_role: membership_test: precursor status is a property of the list, not of the material's role in the process, so the seed tests every input port against Annex I before it considers any attribution. Iron ore concentrates, limestone, coke, coal, natural gas and scrap all fail the test and are inputs with clause-backed exclusions, not precursors
clauses.required_evidence: the definition above plus the Annex I iron and steel cell at S1 offset 144392 that defines the list this good's inputs are tested against
clauses.validation: boundaries/cbam.json segments.precursors.checked_inputs must carry one row per technosphere input with a three state membership value, and goods_complexity must be derived from those rows rather than written as a constant
clauses.acceptance_case: a model that gains an externally purchased ferro-alloy flips the membership reading to listed_precursor, which flips complexity to complex and demands a source pin this repository cannot supply, so the build fails loudly; that path is modeling gap MG-S08

clauses.locator: Annex I, Iron and steel cell, exclusion list
clauses.anchor: 7202 99 80 – Other 7204 – Ferrous waste and scrap; remelting scrap ingots and steel Carbon dioxide
clauses.quote: 7202 99 80 – Other 7204 – Ferrous waste and scrap; remelting scrap ingots and steel Carbon dioxide
clauses.model_role: scrap_membership: heading 7204 appears as one of the entries excluded from the Chapter 72 listing, so ferrous scrap is not a listed good and cannot be a precursor, while 2601 12 00 agglomerated ore is listed in its own right. The seed's scrap input therefore carries carbon through the mass balance and nothing through a precursor rule
clauses.required_evidence: the exclusion list above plus the identical cell in Annex II at S1 offset 150317, plus the count of zero occurrences of 7204 anywhere in the cached S3 text, which is the second independent reading
clauses.validation: the scrap row in checked_inputs must read not_listed with this clause, and no precursor attribution may attach to it
clauses.acceptance_case: a version that treats scrap as a precursor would have to name a source package for scrap, which does not exist and must fail rather than default

clauses.locator: Annex II point E, Monitoring of precursors, same production process branch
clauses.anchor: If the precursors are covered by the same production process in accordance to Article 4(9), only the quantity of additional precursor used and obtained from other installations or from other production processes shall be determined.
clauses.quote: If the precursors are covered by the same production process in accordance to Article 4(9), only the quantity of additional precursor used and obtained from other installations or from other production processes shall be determined.
clauses.model_role: attribution_order: because this seed monitors its five processes as one production process boundary under ST-05, the in-house sinter and hot metal have no additional quantity to determine, so their carbon dioxide is counted once where it is generated and they are not measured as precursors. The other two branches, offsets 180567 and 180988, are the ones that would apply to externally obtained precursors and are recorded as not exercised
clauses.required_evidence: the branch sentence above plus point E's opening rule at offset 179810, the within-installation and other-installation data set lists at 180567 and 180988, the default value fallback at 182365 and the cross-process attribution field at 180747
clauses.validation: precursor_rules.sources must be an empty list, and every in-house transfer port must be disposed of as internal_transfer_netted_inside_the_boundary with its graph counterpart named
clauses.acceptance_case: a transfer port disposed of as a precursor while both endpoints sit inside the monitored boundary is refused by the double counting gate

clauses.locator: Annex II point F, Monitoring of activity levels, off-spec and scrap sentence
clauses.anchor: Off-spec products, by-products, waste, and scrap produced in a production process, irrespective of whether they are returned to production processes, delivered to other installations, or disposed of, shall not be included in the determination of the activity level. They shall therefore be assigned zero embedded emissions when entering another production process.
clauses.quote: Off-spec products, by-products, waste, and scrap produced in a production process, irrespective of whether they are returned to production processes, delivered to other installations, or disposed of, shall not be included in the determination of the activity level. They shall therefore be assigned zero embedded emissions when entering another production process.
clauses.model_role: activity_level_and_denominator: the casting crop is produced by a process of this model, so it is neither in the denominator nor a carrier of embedded emissions. The seed authors it as an output port with a not-applicable disposition and no return edge, which is modeling gap MG-S10
clauses.required_evidence: the off-spec sentence above plus the activity level rule at offset 182797 and the double counting sentence at offset 183036
clauses.validation: exactly one port must be declared the reference product output that carries the functional unit, and every other saleable or discard output outside the counted set must carry a basis; the denominator may not be one of the ports this clause assigns zero to
clauses.acceptance_case: a second denominator owner is refused at freeze time with SEED_BOUNDARY_REFERENCE_PROCESS_UNDECLARED

clauses.locator: Annex I point 2, Table 1, iron and steel rows around the declared good
clauses.anchor: 7202 1 – Ferro-manganese FeMn Carbon dioxide 7202 4 – Ferro-chromium FeCr Carbon dioxide 7202 6 – Ferro-nickel FeNi Carbon dioxide
clauses.quote: 7202 1 – Ferro-manganese FeMn Carbon dioxide 7202 4 – Ferro-chromium FeCr Carbon dioxide 7202 6 – Ferro-nickel FeNi Carbon dioxide
clauses.model_role: counter_evidence_for_scrap: Table 1 does give categories and gases for the ferro-alloys that Annex I excludes from Chapter 72, which shows the exclusion of 7204 in ST-14 is a deliberate reading rather than a formatting accident, and that an externally purchased ferro-alloy would be a listed good and therefore a precursor
clauses.required_evidence: the three alloy rows above plus the pig iron and sinter rows at offset 50803 plus the crude steel row at offset 51389, read against the S1 exclusion list of ST-14
clauses.validation: checked_inputs must state that no listed good enters this model from outside, so goods_complexity stays simple on both the package side and the ledger side
clauses.acceptance_case: the moment a listed good is drawn into the model the two sides disagree with a simple reading and the build stops

clauses.locator: Annex I point 1 definitions (4), (5), (15), (16) and process emission list
clauses.anchor: (a) the chemical, electrolytic or pyrometallurgical reduction of metal compounds in ores, concentrates and secondary materials; (b) the removal of impurities from metals and metal compounds; (c) the decomposition of carbonates, including those used for flue gas cleaning;
clauses.quote: (a) the chemical, electrolytic or pyrometallurgical reduction of metal compounds in ores, concentrates and secondary materials; (b) the removal of impurities from metals and metal compounds; (c) the decomposition of carbonates, including those used for flue gas cleaning;
clauses.model_role: emission_kind_vocabulary: ore reduction and carbonate decomposition are process emissions, not combustion, and carbon monoxide counts as its molar equivalent of carbon dioxide, which is what lets a mass balance ignore oxidation state. The seed labels each counted port with the kind this vocabulary gives it: burden reduction, raceway combustion, carbonate decomposition, converter carbon mass balance and converter flux decomposition
clauses.required_evidence: the three sub bullets above plus definitions (4) at offset 40279, (5) at 40561, (15) at 43253 and (16) at 43483
clauses.validation: every counted port must carry an emission_kind drawn from this vocabulary and a role id in model/roles.json that states which of the listed processes it belongs to
clauses.acceptance_case: a carbonate decomposition port labelled as combustion is a classification error the coverage report exposes, because the basis text and the kind disagree

clauses.locator: Annex I point 3.15.2.2, electric arc furnace branch
clauses.anchor: emitting CO 2 from the consumption of electrodes and electrode pastes;
clauses.quote: emitting CO 2 from the consumption of electrodes and electrode pastes;
clauses.model_role: scope_of_the_other_route: electrode carbon is a source only in the electric arc furnace branch, so the BF-BOF model carries no electrode port at all. Table 5's scrap rows at offset 188137 belong to the activity data side and do not make scrap a listed good
clauses.required_evidence: the electrode bullet above plus the 3.15.2.2 heading at offset 73705 and the Table 5 iron and steel scrap rows at offset 188137
clauses.validation: no port, slot or parameter of this seed may name an electrode; the electric arc furnace route is registered as modeling gap MG-S03 instead of being half modelled
clauses.acceptance_case: a future version that adds an electrode port must also change the production route and would no longer be this package

defects.statement: the crude steel section sends the reader to point B.3.2 of Annex III at S3 offset 73679, while the number B.3.2 occurs exactly once in the whole text, at offset 107951, inside Annex II; Annex III is divided into A, B and C at offsets 190624, 207277 and 213041 and has no point B.3.2. The neighbouring sections do not agree with each other either: pig iron at offset 67649 cites Annex II, crude steel and iron or steel products cite Annex III
defects.consequence: a package that quotes the cross-reference literally looks broken next to one that resolves it, and a reader who searches Annex III for the mass balance method finds nothing
defects.resolution: parameters/carbon-content.json records the quoted string, the offset and the resolution sentence together, so the inconsistency is preserved as evidence rather than silently rewritten; modeling gap MG-S07 tracks it

defects.statement: the hydrogen seed 1.3.0 ledger row for grid electricity records its Annex I membership under the key listed_in_annex_i, which the builder gate does not read, and the gate returns early when the three state membership key is absent, so a listed good is stored as not listed and nothing notices
defects.consequence: an incorrect membership claim ships inside a released seed and its boundary text repeats it
defects.resolution: out of scope for this seed, which uses the three state vocabulary; recorded here so the correction has a documented origin, and tracked in docs/STANDARD_SEED_ENTERPRISE_PERIOD_AND_AUTOLOAD_V1.md section 9

defects.statement: the build gate accepts an end_use object that states no_runtime_declaration_for_this_good whenever the boundary has no undecided item marked runtime_input_required (seeds/standard_seed_bundle.py lines 1843 to 1866), while the trial itself refuses that same state for every good whose calculation is not the three component one (analysis/cbam_trial_v2.py lines 252 to 259, with the message that a direct only good states its end use as a declaration to collect). For a direct only seed the two are mutually exclusive, so the combination passes the build gate and cannot be solved
defects.consequence: a direct only seed whose good has no end use provision in the law would ship green and fail on the first trial request, which is the failure mode the acceptance run exists to catch before shipping
defects.resolution: this seed states a declaration to collect instead, which both layers accept, so no runtime behaviour is changed by this slice; the exclusion is recorded here so that a later direct only good with no textual end use provision has a documented origin for choosing between the two layers rather than inventing a provision to satisfy one of them

defects.statement: the refusal a declared end use raises is named after one sector: analysis/cbam_trial_v2.py line 875 says that hydrogen consumed inside the reporting installation is not a CBAM good, while the branch that reaches it is the generic check that a declared value sits in the package's not_a_cbam_good list
defects.consequence: a crude steel filing that declares further_rolling_or_forging is refused with a sentence about hydrogen, so the panel tells the reporter about the wrong good
defects.resolution: left open by this slice because the acceptance run has to observe the refusal as it is today; the fix is to let the message come from the method package's own wording for that value rather than from a literal in the analysis module

gaps.statement: default values for embedded emissions are stated as a rule but not as numbers in either cached text: S1 offset 62837 defers them to implementing acts, S3 offset 182472 defers to Annex IV of the regulation and Annex V at S3 offset 236165 adapts them per region, while the instrument that carries the values was not retrieved. Which implementing act carries them is not verified, so this mapping does not name one
gaps.consequence: every candidate that would be reported on a default value stays undecided, which is modeling gap MG-S05
gaps.next_step: retrieve the implementing act that publishes the default values, hash it, and attach its table rows to a versioned default value package before any default based result

gaps.statement: the re-fetch attempts of 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22 returned HTTP 202 with an empty body behind an AWS WAF challenge for all four URLs, including the two control URLs, so no hash in this file was re-verified after 2026-09-19. The first version of that report recorded the empty body's own SHA-256, which would have read as a successful retrieval; the fetch script now refuses to enter a non-200 response into the evidence chain and the old report is kept as steel_sources_report.pre-fix-20260921.json
gaps.consequence: the cached texts remain authoring-time evidence with a retrieval date, not a live confirmation that the legal text is unchanged
gaps.next_step: re-run tmp/segment9h_01_eu_fetch_steel.py from a session that clears the challenge and compare hashes before the next seed version bump

gaps.statement: the atomic weights used by the independent derivation of the carbon book (C 12.011, O 15.999, H 1.008, Fe 55.845, Ca 40.078) were transcribed during authoring without a retrieval, a hash or a captured citation
gaps.consequence: the published factor rows and the atomic derivation agree to within 0.0016 per cent for carbon dioxide and 0.065 per cent for the calcium carbonate residue, but the input constants of the second number have no evidence record, so the seed keeps claim_level demonstration
gaps.next_step: attach a published source record with URL, retrieval date and content hash in the shape of the Annex II point G record

gaps.statement: the acceptance engine answers FLOW_PROPERTY_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every exact-version Flow Property resource, so the electricity flow property the seed pins cannot be re-attested on it, while the mass property resolves
gaps.consequence: the two electricity ports of model/graph.json carry a declared identity that the builder checks for completeness and internal consistency, not one the engine has confirmed
gaps.next_step: re-probe the catalog resolve route for flow properties on an engine that exposes the resource and flip attestable_on_current_engine to true only with the observed row

gaps.statement: Annex I membership was tested by searching the candidate CN heading strings in the two cached texts and counting occurrences, not by resolving them against a versioned goods set object, and no chapter-wide comparison of the Section XV and Section VII codes was performed
gaps.consequence: the not_listed readings of ST-13 and ST-14 hold for this seed on that narrower evidence, which is what the checked_inputs limitation row states
gaps.next_step: publish the Annex I goods list as a versioned package with per code rows and test membership against it

modeling_gaps.statement: finishing rolling, coating and other iron or steel products processes are outside the model, which ends at the continuous casting slab
modeling_gaps.consequence: the model is one crude steel route, not a steel plant, and a reader who expects the product of the whole plant sees a low number
modeling_gaps.next_step: model the 3.16 boundary of S3 offset 74694 as a separate seed rather than as extra nodes here

modeling_gaps.statement: the alternative reading of Article 4(9), where sintered ore and hot metal are treated as within-installation cross-process precursors and each carries its own specific embedded emissions, is not implemented: the precursor source pin must name another seed's released package and the gate refuses a source process belonging to this seed
modeling_gaps.consequence: the chosen single boundary reading counts their carbon dioxide once at the process that emits it, which is arithmetically complete but is not the only lawful reading
modeling_gaps.next_step: either publish sintered ore and pig iron as their own seeds, or add an intra-seed precursor source rule to the package contract

modeling_gaps.statement: the electric arc furnace and direct reduced iron routes are not modelled
modeling_gaps.consequence: the production route field is fixed to the blast furnace converter path and the result may not be presented as a route-independent steel figure
modeling_gaps.next_step: a second seed with the 3.15.2.2 boundary, or a multi-route seed once both route parameter sets exist

modeling_gaps.statement: the pre-consumer share of scrap is a declared field with no value and no attribution rule, so no allocation is performed on scrap
modeling_gaps.consequence: scrap carbon enters the mass balance and scrap's upstream burden is outside the boundary; the two are different statements and the boundary file keeps them apart
modeling_gaps.next_step: research the attribution rule before any end-of-life or recycled content claim

modeling_gaps.statement: the default value route cannot be exercised because the numbers are not in any retrieved text, which is gap GS-01
modeling_gaps.consequence: candidates that would be reported on defaults are undecided rather than zero, and the CBAM result refuses while any of them stays open
modeling_gaps.next_step: attach the default value table as a versioned package

modeling_gaps.statement: the organisation and reporting period leg is not part of this seed; no boundaries/organization-ghg.json is authored for crude steel and no period carbon management package is released with it
modeling_gaps.consequence: the same model can serve the three product applications but not an enterprise period inventory, and the CBAM boundary must not be reused as a stand-in for one
modeling_gaps.next_step: add the period layer as a content change, which raises the seed version and keeps the historical reference

modeling_gaps.statement: the Annex III versus Annex II cross-reference defect D-S1 is documented rather than resolved, and the published carbonate factor 0,440 differs from the atomic residue 0.4397118478108826409288012 by 0.065 per cent
modeling_gaps.consequence: two of the eight mass balance residual terms exist only because of that published-versus-atomic difference, so the MFA residual carries them explicitly instead of rounding them away
modeling_gaps.next_step: nothing to resolve in code; the reading is recorded per D-S1

modeling_gaps.statement: no externally purchased listed good enters the model, so the entire external precursor leg is unmodelled: no ferro-alloy, no purchased pig iron, sintered ore or direct reduced iron, and therefore no source identity pin, no default fallback for inconclusive precursor data and no complex goods reading
modeling_gaps.consequence: the seed proves the simple good case only, and the acceptance run cannot claim the external precursor refusal path was exercised on real HTTP because no port reaches it
modeling_gaps.next_step: publish at least one ferro-alloy or pig iron seed with a released specific embedded emissions package, then add the port to this model as a version bump

modeling_gaps.statement: the material streams that are named by the boundary clauses but authored as slots only: the pre-heated blast air with its oxygen, nitrogen and moisture, the lance oxygen, the ore lattice oxygen that leaves with the furnace gas, the secondary metallurgy protective gas, alloy additions and refractory losses, and the flue gas cleaning reagents including the carbonate that ST-18 counts as a process emission
modeling_gaps.consequence: three of the five process nodes close open, and the mass balance residual is explained by eight named terms of which six are exactly these unported oxygen, hydrogen and moisture terms; no closing coefficient is invented
modeling_gaps.next_step: author the air, oxygen and cleaning reagent exchanges when an installation data set exists, which also makes the flue gas carbonate decomposition emission appear

modeling_gaps.statement: the casting crop leaves the boundary as an output with zero embedded emissions and no return edge, so the model is open-ended on that stream rather than a loop
modeling_gaps.consequence: the mass out total includes a stream a real plant re-melts, and the activity level correctly excludes it, which are two different things the boundary files state separately
modeling_gaps.next_step: model the return path together with the activity level rule of ST-16

modeling_gaps.statement: exported blast furnace, coke oven and converter gas is not an authored stream, so the carbon carried out of the boundary in fuel gas is never subtracted
modeling_gaps.consequence: a plant that sells its off-gas shows a lower numerator than this model computes, which biases this seed upward; the slot exists in parameters/activity-data-slots.json with the direction of the bias stated
modeling_gaps.next_step: add the export port and the negative activity row of ST-08's mass balance, then re-derive the carbon book
